topic: How does QoS-driven SINR threshold variation affect congestion control in joint pricing and power allocation schemes?
consensus_response: QoS-driven SINR threshold variation affects congestion control by altering available capacity and resource blocking along calculated paths. Decreased thresholds lead to increased interference, reducing capacity and potentially leading to resource blocking. This can result in admission control failures, as applications may not be able to signal required capacity or QoS requirements other than capacity. Efficient congestion control mechanisms must consider these dynamics to manage available capacity and provide QoS guarantees in satellite networks.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of considering link characteristics, such as latency and jitter, when designing QoS-driven SINR threshold variations. However, it lacks specific data on these metrics.
